Using the standard right-handed basis, \(\mathbf i\times\mathbf j=\mathbf k\). Therefore
\[
(1,0,0)\times(0,1,0)=(0,0,1).
\]

For \(\mathbf a=(a_1,a_2,a_3)\) and \(\mathbf b=(b_1,b_2,b_3)\),
\[
\mathbf a\times\mathbf b=(a_2b_3-a_3b_2,\ a_3b_1-a_1b_3,\ a_1b_2-a_2b_1).
\]
Here \(\mathbf a=(2,1,0)\) and \(\mathbf b=(0,3,4)\), so
\[
\mathbf a\times\mathbf b=(1\cdot4-0\cdot3,\ 0\cdot0-2\cdot4,\ 2\cdot3-1\cdot0).
\]
Thus
\[
\mathbf a\times\mathbf b=(4,-8,6).
\]

First compute the cross product:
\[
(1,2,3)\times(2,0,1)=(2\cdot1-3\cdot0,\ 3\cdot2-1\cdot1,\ 1\cdot0-2\cdot2)=(2,5,-4).
\]
Now take the dot product with \((1,2,3)\):
\[
(2,5,-4)\cdot(1,2,3)=2+10-12=0.
\]
Since the dot product is zero, the cross product is orthogonal to \((1,2,3)\).

questions.prompt: Find the area of the parallelogram spanned by \(\mathbf a=(1,0,2)\) and \(\mathbf b=(0,3,1)\).
questions.answer:
The area of the parallelogram is \(\|\mathbf a\times\mathbf b\|\). Compute the cross product:
\[
\mathbf a\times\mathbf b=(0\cdot1-2\cdot3,\ 2\cdot0-1\cdot1,\ 1\cdot3-0\cdot0)=(-6,-1,3).
\]
Now compute its norm:
\[
\|\mathbf a\times\mathbf b\|=\sqrt{(-6)^2+(-1)^2+3^2}=\sqrt{36+1+9}=\sqrt{46}.
\]
The area is \(\sqrt{46}\).
